dependency_coverage.name: Semiring.toMonoidWithZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts multiplication, identity, zero, and their monoid-with-zero laws from a semiring.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Supports real self-scalar multiplication and its zero behavior.

dependency_coverage.name: SubNegMonoid.toAddMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Extracts the underlying additive monoid from a subtraction-and-negation structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Preserves ordinary addition and zero in the derivative predicates.

binders: For every natural number m, including zero, and every real matrix A indexed by Fin m in both rows and columns.
Assume LocalDef003 A, namely existence of a real eigenvalue family and a real eigenbasis of ℝ^m.
There exist speeds λ : Fin m → ℝ and a basis b of ℝ^m over ℝ indexed by Fin m. These witnesses may depend on m and A and are chosen before, independently of, q, x, and t.
The eigenvector conclusion is quantified over every i ∈ Fin m.
For the same λ and b, the differential equivalence is quantified over every function q : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ^m and every x,t ∈ ℝ.
Inside the right side of that equivalence, every i ∈ Fin m is quantified separately. Its scalar derivative witnesses may depend on q, x, t, i, and the chosen basis.
hypotheses: There exist μ : Fin m → ℝ and a basis e of ℝ^m over ℝ such that A e_i = μ_i e_i for every i ∈ Fin m.
conclusions: There exist a real family λ and a real basis b such that A b_i = λ_i b_i for every i ∈ Fin m.

For this same λ and b, define w_i(ξ,τ) = (b.equivFun(q(ξ,τ)))(i). For every q and every x,t, the following are equivalent: (1) there exist v_t,v_x ∈ ℝ^m such that τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative v_t at t, ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative v_x at x, and v_t + A v_x = 0; (2) for every i, there exist a_i,c_i ∈ ℝ such that τ ↦ w_i(x,τ) has derivative a_i at t, ξ ↦ w_i(ξ,t) has derivative c_i at x, and a_i + λ_i c_i = 0.
mathematical_definitions: Fin m denotes {0,…,m−1}; vectors are real-valued functions on this set, with pointwise vector operations and the finite product topology.
Matrix action is (A v)_j = ∑k∈Fin m A(j,k)v_k.
A basis is a linearly independent spanning family, so each vector v has unique coordinates w with v = ∑i∈Fin m w_i b_i.
b.equivFun maps a vector to these basis coefficients. Thus q(ξ,τ) = ∑i∈Fin m w_i(ξ,τ)b_i.
HasDerivAt asserts existence of the specified ordinary derivative at the given real point. The partial derivatives here are derivatives of separate one-variable slices.
LocalDef001 includes both existence of q_t and q_x at (x,t) and the equation q_t + A q_x = 0.
LocalDef002 includes both existence of the scalar coordinate partial derivatives at (x,t) and the equation (w_i)_t + λ_i(w_i)_x = 0.
LocalDef003 means diagonalizability over the real numbers through a complete real eigenbasis.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Every real square matrix that admits a real eigenbasis admits a choice of real eigenvalues λ_i and real basis vectors b_i satisfying A b_i = λ_i b_i such that the following holds uniformly for every function q of two real variables with values in ℝ^m and every point (x,t). The two partial derivatives of q exist at that point and satisfy q_t + A q_x = 0 if and only if every coefficient w_i of q in the chosen basis has both partial derivatives at that point and satisfies (w_i)_t + λ_i(w_i)_x = 0. The same fixed basis and speeds work for all functions and all points.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The assumption requires a complete real eigenbasis. Merely having real eigenvalues without diagonalizability does not suffice, and matrices requiring complex eigenvalues are outside the asserted implication.
There is no requirement that eigenvalues be distinct, ordered, positive, or nonzero, and no orthogonality or normalization requirement on the basis.

The dimension may be zero. Then all indexed eigenvector and scalar equations are vacuous, the vector space contains only the zero vector, and the vector differential predicate holds for its unique-valued functions.
The functions are defined on all of ℝ × ℝ, and points x and t range over all real numbers. No spatial domain, time half-line, boundary, or initial data are encoded.

No regularity of q is assumed in advance. Each side of the equivalence includes its own derivative-existence requirements; neither side uses a derivative operator that silently assigns a value when differentiation fails.
Even when A or a speed is zero, the corresponding spatial derivative is still required to exist by the predicate.
Only separate partial differentiability at the specified point is required. Joint differentiability, continuity of the partial derivatives, and regularity in a neighborhood are not asserted.
The result is a pointwise equivalence uniformly quantified over all points; it does not assert that an arbitrary q satisfies either differential predicate anywhere.
A, the basis, and the speeds are constant with respect to space and time. No varying coefficient matrix or varying coordinate transformation is included.
No existence or uniqueness of solutions, characteristic formula, propagation theorem, stability estimate, or weak-solution interpretation is encoded.
